verdicts.note: Danish national registry, 458,475 women born 1957-72 followed age 20-45, outcome COMPLETED FAMILY SIZE. The strongest primary-cell record found: a BEHAVIORAL_NET estimand in a controlled-fertility population, which is precisely where the scope doc predicts the effect should vanish.
Lancet stillbirth series: making the data count. No abstract.
Economic and psychosocial consequences of stillbirth.
Lancet series, high-income stillbirth rates and trends.
Lancet series prevention/advocacy piece.
Lancet series progress/advocacy piece.

Chernobyl fallout by Finnish municipality, with live births, stillbirths, pregnancy loss AND induced abortion as outcomes. An exogenous exposure shock with the full outcome set, so the induced/spontaneous separation of Wall 4 is testable here.
1000+ intrauterine deaths, London; contemporary demographic profile.
UK teaching-hospital stillbirth rate by gestation.
Whether fertility treatment itself raises early loss; ART selection, Wall 6.
Preconception cortisol/alpha-amylase and loss; prospective, null.
Depression after miscarriage or stillbirth.
Intergenerational transmission of infertility and pregnancy loss.
Prior losses and quality of life in a later pregnancy.
Women's education and Indian fertility.
Perinatal mortality risk factors, Sikkim; stillbirth and neonatal components not separated.
Reproductive history and osteoporosis.
Mental disorders after loss.
Iranian fertility decline and birth timing; a tempo study (A.11).
Labour-market outcomes around live and non-live births.
Birth seasonality, fetal loss and air temperature, Serbia; weak venue but the seasonality design is unusual.
CODAC cause-of-death classification with placental histopathology.
Consequences of postponed parenthood; maternal age is the identifying variation, so A.15 (Wall 5).
Alcohol and stillbirth, Aarhus cohort.

Demography 1993: Hutterite fecundability by age and parity with frailty modelling. The natural-fertility benchmark the PM cell is scored against, and heterogeneity in fecundability is what makes loss and low fertility correlate without a causal path.
Nigerian referral-hospital stillbirth determinants.
Swedish registers, 9,785 deaths: age, parity, education, smoking against cause-specific stillbirth AND neonatal death, kept separate. Wall 1 respected in the design.
Induced first-trimester abortion and risk of subsequent miscarriage, Shanghai cohort. Sits exactly on Wall 4: A.4's treatment acting through B.5's channel.
Indigenous/non-Indigenous stillbirth disparity, Queensland.

Social Biology 1989: whether gravidity and age drive the fetal-loss gradient, on retrospective Australian pregnancy histories. The parity-to-loss direction the identification caution names as first-order.
Rural Varanasi, 8,111 registered pregnancies: maternal UNDERNUTRITION and pregnancy wastage. The nutrition driver named in B.5's claim, prospectively observed.
Concealed long-QT in a recurrent-loss family; single-family genetics.
Intra-urban fetal mortality by social vulnerability, Sao Paulo.
Pregnancy loss in two Nairobi slums.
Fetal death after COVID mitigation in three Nordic registries; a policy shock on the loss margin with no fertility outcome.
IUFD prevalence, single centre; weak.
Prospective longitudinal fertility, time-to-pregnancy and outcomes after recurrent miscarriage. Measures the recovery process the net-effect calculation needs.
Cousens 2011 worldwide stillbirth estimates; predecessor of the Blencowe anchor.
Population-based prospective conception, early loss and time to clinical pregnancy. No abstract in the index.
WHO multicountry survey; late fetal deaths and early neonatal deaths reported separately.
Alcohol and fetal death (SAB and stillbirth), Danish National Birth Cohort.
US pregnancies and pregnancy rates BY OUTCOME 1976-96 -- the full accounting of conceptions into live birth, induced abortion and fetal loss that a decomposition needs.
Measuring early pregnancy loss: laboratory and field methods. The observation-window problem stated methodologically.

NYC 320,726 births split into late antepartum fetal death, intrapartum fetal death, and neonatal death, by maternal age and parity. Decomposes across the live-birth boundary, which is what Wall 1 needs and what perinatal composites usually prevent.
Stress and early pregnancy loss. No abstract.
PartoMa labour-management guidelines, quasi-experimental.
Parental chromosomal abnormality and the pattern of repeated miscarriage.
Prospective population-based early pregnancy loss in Karnataka, separating miscarriage from medically terminated pregnancy. Wall 4 handled explicitly in a low-resource setting.
Fertility after recurrent miscarriage, 719 couples; subsequent reproductive outcome given a loss history.
